title: Install the lightweight flywheel, the clutch and the release bearing
imprint: Aasco installation instructions p.2-4; Fastening Specifications 996 p.19, p.81

notices.text: Flywheel steps and torques from the Aasco installation instructions, pages 2 to 4. Pressure plate torque from the torque book page 81 item 4. The WSM covers the dual-mass flywheel only.

Never reuse flywheel bolts. Use the kit bolts. Check the length of every bolt before the flywheel goes on (step 4). A bolt that bottoms in the crankshaft gives a false torque reading and the flywheel comes loose.
Do not use an impact driver on the flywheel bolts or the pressure plate bolts.
Keep threadlocker off the flywheel face and the crankshaft flange. Apply it to the bolt thread only, one bolt at a time, after the first pass.

The flywheel bolt torque is 75 Nm (55 ft-lb) for an M10 x 1.0 bolt per the Aasco guide. The SSF catalogue note says 60 ft-lb. The manufacturer sheet governs. The OEM 25 Nm + 90° is for the dual-mass flywheel bolt only.

The Aasco sheet asks for new disc, pressure plate and release bearing with the flywheel. The Aasco 106411-11 comes with the pilot bearing, the bolts and the torque plate. The torque plate must be used.

steps.text: Clean the rust preventive from the flywheel with brake cleaner. Clean the friction face until a white cloth stays clean. (Aasco p.2)
Set the old flywheel on the new one with the bolt holes aligned. Make sure that the sensor teeth are in the same position. (Aasco p.2)
Make sure that the crankshaft flange is clean and dry. Make sure that the rear main seal is dry. Press the new pilot bearing into the crankshaft. (Aasco p.2-3)
Thread one kit bolt into the crankshaft to the stop. Measure the depth B. Measure the flywheel and the torque plate together, A. Record A minus B. The minimum is 2.0 mm (0.080 in). (Aasco p.3)
Put the flywheel on the crankshaft with the torque plate. Lock the flywheel. Tighten all 8 bolts dry to 27 Nm in a cross pattern. (Aasco p.3)
Remove one bolt. Apply threadlocker to its thread. Refit it and tighten to 27 Nm. Do the same with each of the other 7 bolts, one at a time. (Aasco p.4)
Tighten all 8 bolts to 75 Nm in a cross pattern. Make a paint mark on each bolt head. (Aasco p.4)
Centre the clutch disc on the flywheel with the alignment tool. Put the pressure plate on the dowel pins. Tighten the 6 bolts by hand in turns until the plate is seated. (Aasco p.4)
Tighten the pressure plate bolts to 23 Nm in a cross pattern. Remove the alignment tool. (torque book p.81)
Examine the release bearing guide sleeve for a wear step. Replace it if there is a step. Fit the new release bearing. Take photographs before the transmission goes on.

specs.name: Flywheel bolt free thread clearance in the crankshaft, A minus B

spec_note: Aasco gives a minimum of 0.080 to 0.100 in (2.0 to 2.5 mm) of free clearance. The 6 mm upper bound is a sanity limit, not from the sheet: more than that means the bolt is too short for full thread engagement.
